transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Solutions), Elena Rodriguez (Head of ML, Nimbus), Marcus Holt (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (CTO), Aamir Khan (Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focused on search/retrieval-augmented generation for Nimbus Finance internal analytics workflows. Main topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and timeline/milestones (kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout).

Topics:
- Success criteria: latency, cost per request, and QA/quality regression thresholds on top-k retrieved contexts
- Workload sizing: concurrency, tokens per request, corpus size for benchmarks
- Benchmarks: baseline with current model (on-prem), Redwood hosted + dedicated profiles
- Timeline & milestones: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45-60 min, we wanna lock scope on the POC milestones and what success looks like, Jordan's gonna go through benchmarking approach, Samir will cover ops and credentials, and then we can align on timeline.
[00:22] Elena: Great, yes thanks. We have a hard timeline - board wants an exec readout late October, end of month. Ideally we validate cost/lantency and a quality gate that we can present.
[00:40] Marcus: Our baseline currently runs on a mix of on-prem GPUs; throughput is low, p95 latencies around 800-1,200ms for 1k token prompt with retrieval. We're constrained on concurrency, so we want to understand Redwood dedicated vs hosted economics.
[01:05] Jordan: cool, so for the POC we're proposing a 4-week engagement: kickoff, access/setup, a mid-point review at ~2 weeks with preliminary benchmarks, and an exec readout at week 4. Benchmarks will include P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens simulation, and accuracy/QA on a labeled holdout set.
[01:34] Priya: When you say accuracy/QA, what's the metric? We're mainly worried about RAG hallucination rate and retrieval relevance.
[01:45] Jordan: good call. We'll use a combined metric set: retrieval nDCG@10 on your relevance labels, plus a human-eval pass on a 150-example set for hallucination/precision. We'll surface automatic metrics and a small manual sample for exec.
[02:10] Aamir: From security side, we need SOC two artifacts, KMS integration details, audit logs retention and RBAC controls. Also need to confirm whether any data leaves our VPC in hosted mode.
[02:30] Maya: totally, we'll share SOC2 and security pack. For hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit; we can discuss a VPC/private deployment for sensitive data. Jordan, can you list the network checklist?
[02:45] Jordan: yes, the checklist: VPC peering or private link, IAM principals, S3 access patterns for ingest, and a small test dataset link. We'll provide infra docs and a test harness repo.
[03:05] Elena: Sounds good. For workload sizing: our typical queries are 600-1,200 tokens including retrieved context, average 850 tokens. Peak concurrent users about 80, but typical steady-state concurrency ~25. Monthly usage estimate for POC-like workload about 12M tokens.
[03:30] Jordan: perfect, that's helpful. For benching we'll run these scenarios: cold-start latency, warmed KV-cache throughput, batched vs single-request. We'll run with two model profiles: an open Llama-variant quantized profile and a larger high-quality variant to compare cost/quality tradeoffs.
[03:58] Marcus: Can you give an example SLO for us to validate?
[04:05] Jordan: a proposed SLO: P95 latency < 800ms for single-request path at target concurrency 25, and cost per 1M tokens under $X (we'll put concrete number in the SOW). Also quality drop no more than 5% relative to your baseline on our eval metric.
[04:25] Elena: That P95 target seems reasonable; our baseline p95 is ~1.1s so anything under 800ms will be a win.
[04:38] Maya: ok next milestone planning. Proposed dates: kickoff week of 2025-09-22, access/setup complete by 2025-09-26, mid-point review on 2025-10-06, exec readout 2025-10-24. Does that align with your internal timeline?
[04:58] Priya: yes exec readout on 10/24 lines up, leaves us time to prepare slides.
[05:08] Marcus: Access/setup - we'll need a list of exact network ingress IPs, and we'll create a test S3 bucket with sanitized data by 9/24.
[05:20] Jordan: we'll provide the IPs and the infra checklist today; you'll share access details by 9/24. For benchmark harness: we'll run 3 runs across 3 different model configs and send raw metrics + analysis.
[05:40] Elena: On acceptance criteria, besides latency and cost we want: 1) integration works with our auth flow, 2) no PII leakage in logs, 3) reproducible benchmark results.
[05:55] Samir: Ops note — for dedicated we can provision a reserved pool that mirrors production memory and GPU type; for private deployment we have a package that runs in customer VPC but requires a little more lead time. We'll call that out in the SOW.
[06:15] Aamir: If we want private, what's the timeline delta?
[06:22] Samir: private deployment typically adds 2-3 weeks for network approvals and KMS/HSM integration; for the POC we recommend hosted with VPC peering to shorten timeline unless you require private from day one.
[06:40] Elena: We want to evaluate both but prioritize hosted + VPC for speed.
[06:48] Jordan: ok noted. About benchmarks and dataset: we'll need a 150-item labeled eval set for human checks and ~10k query simulation corpus for load tests. Marcus, can you confirm we can generate that?
[07:03] Marcus: yes we'll assemble and share by 9/24. We may have to scrub some fields but doable.
[07:12] Priya: any concerns about cost for Redwood during the POC? I want to make sure we're not surprised.
[07:18] Maya: the POC pricing is capped; we'll include a not-to-exceed figure in the SOW and a breakdown per model profile so you can compare hosted vs dedicated.
[07:30] Jordan: on the benchmark plan we'll simulate sustained concurrency of 25 and short spikes to 80 to understand queuing and autoscaling behavior. We'll measure tokens/sec and total cost for each run.
[07:47] Elena: For exec readout, would it be possible for Redwood to provide a slide deck with topline metrics and recommended next steps?
[07:55] Maya: yes we'll prepare a concise exec deck with topline benchmarks, cost tradeoffs, and recommended production path (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[08:06] Marcus: How will we validate quality/regression automatically?
[08:12] Jordan: we'll run auto-evals like nDCG and a few simple heuristics, then a small manual review on the 150 sample set. We'll flag any regressions >5% and discuss root cause.
[08:26] Aamir: Security checklist follow-up: need an NDA addendum for certain data, plus details on log retention and whether Pinecone or any third party embedding store will be used.
[08:40] Maya: noted, we'll include the NDA addendum and note on embedding store recommendations. Jordan, include recommended embed store options.
[08:49] Jordan: will do — we'll list Redwood's supported embed stores and guidance.
[09:00] Maya: let's recap milestones and owners: Kickoff (week of 9/22) - Maya to schedule; Access/setup (by 9/26) - Marcus provides creds; Benchmarking run (9/29-10/03) - Jordan; Mid-point review (10/06) - internal review + preliminary results; Exec readout (10/24) - joint slides.
[09:25] Elena: yep that works. Can you send SOW and checklist today?
[09:30] Maya: I'll send SOW and pricing by end of day 9/15, Jordan will share benchmark plan and repo link 9/16.
[09:40] Priya: ok once we have the SOW we'll loop in procurement and legal for the NDA and PO.
[09:48] Marcus: small technical question — does Redwood support KV cache warmup scripts? We want to test warmed-up latency.
[09:55] Jordan: yes we have scripts to pre-populate KV cache and measure warmed vs cold path; we'll include that in the harness.
[10:05] Elena: any last questions?
[10:10] Aamir: just confirm that audit logs retention configurable to 1 year and KMS keys remain with us.
[10:16] Maya: yes we'll include options; for hosted we can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed keys, and logs retention configurable. We'll detail in the security pack.
[10:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with SOW, security docs, and schedule kickoff.
[10:40] Elena: thanks all.
[10:45] End of call.

Recap (as stated on call):
- POC length: ~4 weeks (kickoff week of 2025-09-22 to exec readout 2025-10-24)
- Milestones: Kickoff, Access/setup (VPC + creds), Benchmark runs, Mid-point review, Exec readout
- Success criteria: P95 latency < 800ms at 25 concurrency, cost per 1M tokens within capped budget, quality drop <= 5% on eval metric, secure network & KMS integration
- Immediate next steps: SOW, benchmark plan, customer to provide sanitized sample data and VPC details

References / Links mentioned:

- Security pack and SOC2 - link to be shared by Maya
